have he : permutationLinear π-permutationLinear ρ=
      (permutationLinear π-permutationLinear σ)+(permutationLinear σ-permutationLinear ρ) := by abel
  rw [he]
findings.problem: The proof states the telescoping identity a - c = (a - b) + (b - c) as a separate `have`, proves it with `abel`, and then rewrites with it. Mathlib already has this identity under a descriptive name, so the helper step and the `abel` call are not needed.
findings.proposed_change:
unfold permutationDistance
  rw [← sub_add_sub_cancel (permutationLinear π) (permutationLinear σ) (permutationLinear ρ)]
  exact (Submodule.finrank_mono (LinearMap.range_add_le _ _)).trans
    (Submodule.finrank_add_le_finrank_add_finrank _ _)
findings.benefit: This removes a three-line helper and an `abel` call. The lemma name `sub_add_sub_cancel` states the key idea directly: split the difference through σ. The rest of the argument stays the same. The range of a sum lies in the sum of the ranges, and finrank is subadditive. The proof is shorter and just as clear.

findings.excerpt:
induction h with
  | rel a b hab =>
    obtain ⟨k,rfl,rfl⟩ := hab
    exact congrFun hf k
  | refl a => rfl
  | symm a b h ih => exact ih.symm
  | trans a b c h₁ h₂ ih₁ ih₂ => exact ih₁.trans ih₂
findings.problem: The proof does a full four-case induction over `EqvGen`, and three of the cases (refl, symm, trans) are boilerplate. They just re-prove that `f x = f y` is an equivalence relation. Mathlib already packages this as the universal property of the generated equivalence (`Setoid.eqvGen_le`), applied to the kernel setoid `Setoid.ker f`.
findings.proposed_change:
theorem matching_respects {ι β : Type*} {π σ : Equiv.Perm ι} (f : ι → β)
    (hf : f ∘ π=f ∘ σ) {i j : ι} (h : matchingSetoid π σ i j) : f i=f j :=
  Setoid.eqvGen_le (s := Setoid.ker f) (by rintro _ _ ⟨k, rfl, rfl⟩; exact congrFun hf k) h
findings.benefit: The proof now states its idea directly: the kernel of f is an equivalence relation that contains every generating pair (π k, σ k), so it contains the equivalence they generate. The only real step, `congrFun hf k`, stays visible. The refl/symm/trans boilerplate disappears and nothing new is hidden.
